description: COMPUTER ARCHITECTURE: the organisation of a digital processor — CPU, registers, cache, pipeline, ALU, instruction set, memory hierarchy. A modern-region anchor (post-1885 computing, foreign to Cornelius Vane's Victorian frame).

microtheory.name: computer_architecture
microtheory.definition: The organisation and design of a digital computer's processor and memory: the CPU's datapath and control, the register file, the cache and memory hierarchy, the arithmetic-logic unit, the instruction set, and the clocked bus that ties them together. The modern computing world Cornelius Vane has no concept of.

concepts.name: cpu
concepts.definition: The central processing unit — the processor that fetches, decodes and executes instructions.

concepts.name: register
concepts.definition: A small, fast storage cell inside the CPU holding an operand or address.

concepts.name: cache
concepts.definition: A small fast memory holding recently-used data, bridging the CPU-memory speed gap.

concepts.name: pipeline
concepts.definition: Overlapping the fetch/decode/execute stages of successive instructions for throughput.

concepts.name: alu
concepts.definition: The arithmetic-logic unit — the CPU circuit that computes arithmetic and logic operations.

concepts.name: instruction_set
concepts.definition: The vocabulary of machine operations a processor implements (the ISA).

concepts.name: memory_hierarchy
concepts.definition: The tiered store — registers, cache, RAM, disk — trading speed for capacity.

concepts.name: transistor
concepts.definition: The semiconductor switch from which all digital logic gates are built.

concepts.name: clock
concepts.definition: The periodic signal that paces a synchronous processor's operations.

concepts.name: bus
concepts.definition: The shared set of wires carrying data, addresses and control between components.

concepts.name: control_unit
concepts.definition: The CPU block that sequences the datapath by decoding instructions into control signals.

concepts.name: program_counter
concepts.definition: The register holding the address of the next instruction to fetch.

concepts.name: opcode
concepts.definition: The field of a machine instruction that names the operation to perform.

concepts.name: word_size
concepts.definition: The native bit-width a processor operates on (8, 16, 32, 64 bits).

concepts.name: cache_line
concepts.definition: The fixed-size block of memory a cache loads and evicts as a unit.

concepts.name: datapath
concepts.definition: The functional units and buses through which data flows and is transformed in a CPU.

concepts.name: interrupt
concepts.definition: A signal that diverts the processor to service an asynchronous event.

concepts.name: addressing_mode
concepts.definition: A rule for computing an operand's memory address from an instruction.

concepts.name: microcode
concepts.definition: The low-level control words that implement a complex instruction inside the CPU.

concepts.name: branch_predictor
concepts.definition: The unit that guesses a conditional branch's outcome to keep the pipeline full.
